title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Atractylis separates cited ingestion from an attributed holding-and-release claim
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the complete Lonitzer 1551 Atractylis entry, crushed leaves, flower-tops and seed taken with pepper and wine are said to help against scorpion stings, explicitly citing Dioscorides. The next sentence starts `Sunt qui dicant` and gives a different route and a two-state consequence: some say a scorpion-bitten person feels no pain while holding the plant, but is affected by pain after putting it down. The attribution belongs to the full holding/release contrast; the source reports no directly observed efficacy. Do not merge ingestion and possession into one verified cure or gloss the cited and anonymous claims as interchangeable. The source is a preserved typed 1551 edition display, not a modern clinical report or proof of medieval manuscript transmission. No Voynich target/forms/meaning are assigned. Duplicate checks are navigation, not novelty proof.

design.mechanism: An anonymous report scopes over a conditional possession-state contrast (pain absent while the herb is held, pain present after it is put down), distinct from a separately Dioscorides-cited oral preparation for scorpion stings.
design.unit: The complete Atractylis entry in the retained Lonitzer 1551 text, especially the medicinal section and its transition from the Dioscorides-cited operation to `Sunt qui dicant`.
design.contrast: Preserve source attribution and different administration mode: cited ingestion versus unnamed reported holding/release. The rival flattening treats both as one directly observed antivenom result or lets the report frame describe only the first local action.
design.prediction: Any future fixed content candidate must keep the cited oral action separate from the full anonymous holding/pain-return condition, and must mark the latter as reported rather than observed; a bare protection/cure noun does not encode these distinctions.
design.scope: Exploratory content hypothesis only; target meaning unbound, no target forms assigned, not a selected experiment.

source_evidence.quote: Atractylidis folia, coma et semen, trita, cum pipere vinoque pota, contra scorpionum ictus prosunt, teste Dioscoride. Sunt qui dicant a scorpionibus percussos, quam diu eam herbam teneeant, non sentire dolorem, deposita vero dolore af fici.
